title: The Good German
full_review:
"The Good German" (Warner Bros.) is the compelling, albeit somewhat contrived, story of Jake Geismer (George Clooney), a U.S. war correspondent who comes to Berlin to cover the Potsdam peace conference after World War II. Here, the Allied forces would oversee the disarming of Germany, now a landscape of bombed-out ruins.

In short order, he finds Lena Brandt (Cate Blanchett), the married German woman with whom he once had an affair and who is now desperate to leave the country, and he attempts to rekindle their romance.

He also attempts to solve the mystery of the murder of the opportunistic young Cpl. Tully (Tobey Maguire) assigned to be his driver. This eventually leads him to Lena's scientist husband, Emile, whose expertise is sought by both the American and Russian occupiers, despite his probable involvement in Nazi war crimes.

Everyone is harboring secrets, moral complexities abound and the "truth" is frustratingly elusive. The film ultimately makes vividly clear the desperate and immoral methods by which many survived during the war, and then the widespread corruption that ensued in the postwar period.

Clooney is solid as ever, Blanchett pulls off her faux-Marlene Dietrich accent, Maguire is appropriately despicable, and there's good work from Beau Bridges and Leland Orser as the principal American military leaders, and Ravil Isyanov as a Russian general.

Director Steven Soderbergh has filmed this adaptation of Joseph Kanon's novel with the black-and-white back-lot trappings of actual postwar films such as "A Foreign Affair" and "The Third Man," including the camera angles, rear projections and insistent musical score that would have been used at the time. This stunt, however cleverly executed, sometimes calls attention to itself (as in the "Casablanca"-like fade-out), but nonetheless is more successful than not.

Despite the retro techniques employed, the adult themes, sexual content and language are very much in the contemporary vein, though by today's standards they're reasonably restrained.

The film contains rough language and profanity, crude expressions, racial epithets, prostitution, a shadowy sexual encounter without nudity, adultery, rape discussion, violence, murder and a mild striptease. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
